summary: Defines a USER_ERROR_SPEC object for RSVP so that applications and implementers can report user-defined errors. The existing ERROR_SPEC object has a limited set of error codes, and the convention has been to add new ones sparingly, with no provision for user-defined errors. This new object is used in addition to the existing one.

plainLanguage.summary: A form with only a few fixed complaint boxes is not much use when something odd happens. This adds a free-form box where users can describe their own kind of problem.

questions: how to define custom rsvp errors
subtitle: A new RSVP object that lets implementers carry their own error codes and descriptions.

tldr.problem: RSVP's ERROR_SPEC object allows only 256 error codes, new codes are added sparingly, and there is no provision for user-defined errors.
tldr.mechanism: A new error code, 33 (User Error Spec), signals that a USER_ERROR_SPEC object (class 194, C-Type 1) is present, carrying an enterprise number, a user error value, an optional description and optional subobjects.
tldr.outcome: Organizations can define their own errors for debugging and testing, and can share them to help interoperability, without changing the mandatory contents of RSVP error messages.

today: RFC 5284 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2008. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why User-Defined Errors
sections.content:
The Resource ReserVation Protocol (RSVP, RFC 2205) reports errors in an ERROR_SPEC object. Its format permits 256 error codes. As RSVP has been extended, the convention has been to be conservative about defining new ones, and there is no provision for user-defined errors.

When developing RSVP extensions, it is often useful to define error messages to help with initial debugging and with testing against older versions or other implementations. This RFC lets organizations define errors for internal development, which could also be shared with the wider community to promote interoperability.

RSVP PathErr and ResvErr messages, and the Notify message from RFC 3473, must carry an ERROR_SPEC. To avoid changing that, a new error code says that the new object is present. The ResvConf message also carries an ERROR_SPEC, but without meaningful codes, so these extensions do not apply to it.
sections.plainLanguage: RSVP only knows a short list of things that can go wrong. Teams building new features need a way to say 'something specific to my work went wrong'.

sections.title: The USER_ERROR_SPEC Object
sections.content:
A new Error Code, 33 (User Error Spec), is used in an ERROR_SPEC to signal a USER_ERROR_SPEC. One Error Value is defined: 0, meaning further details are in the User Error Spec. When sending this code, a USER_ERROR_SPEC MUST be included in the PathErr, ResvErr or Notify message.

The object is Class = 194, C-Type = 1. Its class number is in the range 192-247 for backward compatibility: implementations that do not understand such an object forward it unmodified. Its fields are:

  • Enterprise Number: a 32-bit identifier of an organization, assigned by IANA in its Enterprise Numbers registry.
  • Sub Org: an 8-bit value that lets an organization create independent Error Value spaces for parallel teams. If not needed, it SHOULD be zero.
  • Err Desc Len: the length in bytes of the description, excluding padding. Zero is valid.
  • User Error Value: a 16-bit integer whose meaning is set by the (sub-)organization.
  • Error Description: a string padded with nulls to a multiple of 4 bytes.
  • User-Defined Subobjects: optional extra data.
sections.plainLanguage: Each company gets its own numbered notebook for errors. The object says which company wrote the note, what number the error is, and adds a short sentence in words.

sections.title: Description Text and Subobjects
sections.content:
The Error Description MUST use UTF-8/Net-Unicode encoding (RFC 5198, following the guidance of RFC 2277). Implementations are RECOMMENDED to limit generated strings to single-line printable US-ASCII where feasible. Because the text may not be displayed everywhere, it SHOULD be limited to supplementary information and SHOULD NOT contain information critical to operating the network. Critical information belongs in the User Error Value.

Each subobject is a type-length-value (TLV) with an 8-bit Type assigned by the (sub-)organization and a Length covering the whole subobject including the Type and Length fields. The Length MUST be at least 4 and MUST be a multiple of 4. The meaning of the value is defined by the organization identified by the Enterprise Number and Sub Org.
sections.plainLanguage: The words are a helpful note, but the number is what counts. Anything important goes in the number, since the note may not show up on every screen.

sections.title: Sending and Receiving Procedures
sections.content:
A USER_ERROR_SPEC MAY be included in any PathErr, ResvErr or Notify message for any defined error code, and the Enterprise Number MUST be a valid IANA-assigned value. An ERROR_SPEC with a valid code must still be in every such message. If no other code applies, the code MUST be set to User Error Spec, and the Error Value SHOULD be set to 0.

Receivers are RECOMMENDED to log at least the Enterprise Number, Sub Org, User Error Value and Error Description, and those that can interpret the contents SHOULD act on the error. Implementations that are not UTF-8 capable SHOULD handle the description as described in RFC 5137.

A message with the User Error Spec code but no USER_ERROR_SPEC object, or a USER_ERROR_SPEC on any message other than PathErr, ResvErr or Notify, MUST be treated as malformed and handled according to RFC 2205.

Implementations SHOULD ignore repeated occurrences of the object and SHOULD forward it unchanged on messages they forward, for forward compatibility.
sections.plainLanguage: When you get one of these notes, write it down and pass it along unchanged. If the form says 'see attached note' but nothing is attached, treat it as a mistake.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: From the RSVP Error Codes and Globally-Defined Error Value Sub-Codes registry, Error Code 33 (User Error Spec) is assigned, with Error Value sub-code 0 (Further details in User Error Spec). From the RSVP Class Names, Class Numbers, and Class Types registry, Class Number 194 is assigned to USER_ERROR_SPEC, with Class Type 1 named User-Defined Error.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list of codes got two new entries so nobody else uses the same numbers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
This RFC makes no changes to the basic message exchanges of RFC 2205 and RFC 3473. It will cause a small increase in error messages in cases where messages were previously silently dropped for lack of a suitable error code. The mechanism may also be used to report extra error conditions arising from security issues and attacks on the RSVP network.

Displaying or logging a character string opens the way to attacks using overruns or embedded control characters. Implementations SHOULD take precautions against overruns and, especially where the full character set of RFC 5198 is not supported, SHOULD use the procedures in RFC 5137 for unexpected or unknown control characters.
sections.plainLanguage: Text sent by someone else might contain tricks, so be careful when you print it. Do not trust it blindly.

fields.name: Sub Org
fields.desc: Creates independent Error Value spaces; zero if not needed.

fields.name: Err Desc Len
fields.desc: Length of the description in bytes, excluding padding.
